execution_context.file_location: maliciously crafted .diagcab file processed by Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Path traversal in .diagcab allows copying an executable to the Windows Startup folder.
malicious_snippets.code_language: n/a (exploit via crafted file, not direct code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user opens a malicious .diagcab file, the MSDT processes the file and, due to a path traversal flaw, copies an attacker-supplied executable into the Windows Startup folder, resulting in code execution on next reboot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Copying executables to the Startup folder via a support diagnostic file is not expected and enables persistent code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal .diagcab files are for diagnostics, not for writing executables to Startup.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate installers may place shortcuts in Startup, but not via diagnostic files.
key_indicators: Executable dropped from a support file

attack_chain.action: Victim receives and opens a malicious .diagcab file.
attack_chain.leads_to: MSDT processes the file and copies a malicious executable to the Startup folder.

attack_chain.action: Malicious executable runs on next system reboot, achieving code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent access to the system.

behavioral_signatures: MSDT processing .diagcab files resulting in file writes to Startup folder
Unexpected executables appearing in Startup after .diagcab file opened
file_indicators: Presence of unknown executables in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup after .diagcab file opened
Suspicious .diagcab files with path traversal payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for MSDT or related processes writing files to the Startup folder, especially following the opening of .diagcab files. Flag .diagcab files containing path traversal sequences or referencing the Startup folder. Alert on new executables in Startup that are not associated with legitimate software installations.
